content.comment_body: Hi [user_name], I'm having trouble understanding how a counter value gets assigned to a VMx memory word.
You should use the Parameter VM Mapping feature. Navigate to: Tools > Parameter VM Mapping

Check out the attached example for guidance on using counter values. It's best practice to use the counter’s own parameters for digital outputs rather than comparing with analog values outside, since their formats differ and may not match counter values. Regards, [user_name]

The attachment provides a method for comparing values of two up/down counters using Parameter VM Mapping. Scenarios covered include: - Counter 1 is greater than Counter 2 - Counter 2 is greater than Counter 1 - Both counters are equal
That's an interesting approach with 26 blocks, but I actually prefer the attached version that only uses 7 blocks.

Thanks! I've discovered another way that’s more readable. You can use the gray connectors in the diagram editor to link block parameters after expanding each block. I’ve attached a "heating control + setpoint" example in case someone finds it helpful.

You quoted me without referencing your original question to [user_name], which makes my comment unclear. Your actual question concerned retrieving a counter value from the VM memory, not how to reference a counter value in another block.
